title: How to Hand Off an Intercom Chatbot Conversation to a Human
summary: Set up chatbot-to-human handoff in Intercom Messenger with Quickchat AI. See the AI release a chat, claim it in Inbox and verify the customer gets your reply.
body_markdown:
“Can I collect my bike on Friday instead? Please pass this to a person.” Quickchat AI had just told our rider that Saturday pickup at Wheelhouse Repair runs from 10:00 to 13:00. Only the shop could approve a Friday pickup. I claimed the conversation in Intercom Inbox and asked what time the rider had in mind. In the rider’s Messenger, **Piotr joined the conversation** appeared above my reply.


*The handoff from both sides. The rider sees my name and my question in Messenger. The shop sees the same message and my name under Assignee.*


To build this **chatbot-to-human handoff in Intercom Messenger** , connect Quickchat AI as a dedicated teammate. Leave **Reply to all conversations** off, enable **Offer human handoff to Intercom admins** and turn on the Agent’s **Human Handoff** action. When the AI releases the chat, a teammate can claim it in Inbox and send a public **Reply** . You’ll try both sides and see who gets the rider’s next message.


**Already connected?** Start with thefour channel settings andassign the first pickup question . If your team already takes over chats, go straight to thesame-question test to check whether the AI stays quiet after a person claims one.


## 1. How do you set up Intercom Messenger for a handoff test?


Use **one test workspace, two Intercom teammates and a separate visitor** . One teammate signs the AI’s replies. The other takes over as the shop owner. Keep these three browser sessions open as you work. You’ll also need a Quickchat AI account with credits for a few replies.


Who you’re acting as What you’ll do in that window


**Shop owner (Piotr)** Create the Intercom workspace, invite the AI teammate, then claim the Friday request in Inbox.


**AI teammate (Quickchat AI)** Accept the invitation in a second browser profile. Open Quickchat AI in the same profile so Intercom can authorize the right teammate.


**Rider** Open the bike shop in a third browser profile. Send every Friday message from this same Messenger thread.


### Create a workspace you can recognize


1. In the **owner’s** fresh browser profile, start an **Essential** trial with a work address you control. If you already manage customer workspaces, use an address that has never joined them. Our 14-day trial included Messenger, Inbox and both full seats. Intercom asks for a payment method when you buy a plan.[Start the Intercom trial](https://www.intercom.com/signup/email?solution_id=28) ·[Trial terms](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/891) ·[Full seats](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/8205716-seats)


In the form on the left, enter the owner’s work address and select Continue.


1. Choose **Continue** , open the verification email in the same profile, set a password and complete the company profile with your business details. Name the demo workspace **Wheelhouse Repair** .
2. On the getting-started screen, open **Profile** at the bottom left and hover over **Workspace** . Check that **Wheelhouse Repair** is selected before inviting anyone. Keep this owner profile open for the human reply later.


Start at Profile in the bottom left. Hover over Workspace and look for the check beside Wheelhouse Repair.


### Give Quickchat AI its own Intercom login


1. Click **Invite teammates** . From the compact Inbox, use the bottom-left **Settings** gear, then **Workspace → Teammates** . Our trial had a **+ New teammate** menu at the top right. On versions labeled **Add new** , choose **Add new teammates** . Enter a second work address you control and click **Continue and set permissions** .[Invite a teammate](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/280-add-remove-delete-or-export-a-teammate)


Find Teammates under Workspace in the Settings sidebar. The + New teammate menu is at the upper right. Open Invited to see outstanding invitations.


1. On **Set permissions** , choose **Full seat** , which our trial marked **Free during trial** . Give the teammate access to the demo conversations and **Can install, configure and delete apps** under **Apps and integrations** . If the invitation shortcut skips permissions, you can check them later under **Settings → Workspace → Teammates** . Click **Send Invite** .[App installation permissions](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/176-teammate-permissions-how-to-control-workspace-access)


Select Full seat in the left column. Check Conversation access and the other permissions on the right, then use Send Invite at the top.


The trial screenshot also shows **Unlimited usage** under **Copilot** . Copilot is a separate option for people working in Intercom Inbox. You can leave it off for the AI teammate. Quickchat AI will answer the rider through the channel you connect in step 2.[Intercom’s Copilot options](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/9121384-copilot-included-and-unlimited-usage)


1. In a second browser or browser profile, open **Join your team** from the invitation email and sign in with the invited address. Keep the owner signed in to the first browser. While the invitation is outstanding, the owner can find it in **Invited** with the status **Pending signup** . After acceptance, refresh the **Teammates** tab. Our roster then showed two **Active** teammates, each with a **Full** seat.[Accept an Intercom invitation](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/7169398-accept-an-invite-to-an-intercom-workspace)


After acceptance, switch from Invited to Teammates. Read the Status and Seat columns for the two teammates.


1. In the **invited teammate’s browser** , open **Profile** at the bottom left.


In the invited teammate’s browser, click Profile at the bottom of the left sidebar, just below Settings.


Check that **Wheelhouse Repair** is selected, then click your **name or avatar** at the top of the menu. You can also reach the same page through **Settings → Personal → Details** .


Click the row with your avatar at the top of the menu, directly above Away mode.


1. Under **You → Public profile** , click **Edit** . In the first field, beside the person icon and above the email address, enter **Quickchat AI** . Click **Done** and refresh the owner’s **Teammates** list. This is the name you’ll search for under **Assign to** .[Change your Intercom profile name](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/8771110-getting-started-faqs#h_8af298b1a7)


Under Personal → Details, edit the first field in Public profile, beside the person icon. Enter Quickchat AI, then choose Done on that same card.


A **customer-facing alias** changes what visitors see. To make **Quickchat AI** searchable in the assignment picker, edit the ordinary teammate profile name shown above.[How Intercom displays aliases](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/10576050-how-to-use-teammate-alias)


If an invitation is blocked by a **workspace review** notice, Intercom can pause teammate invites while it verifies the business and its Messenger installation. For a standard workspace under review it expects Messenger on a publicly accessible site. A company-controlled demo page is a suitable place to install it. The local address below is for trying the conversation on your own computer.[Intercom workspace review](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/567399-intercom-s-workspace-review-process)


### Put a visitor Messenger on the shop page


1. [Download the Wheelhouse test page and message script](https://quickchat.ai/blog-assets/downloads/wheelhouse-handoff-kit.zip) and unzip them. In the **owner’s Intercom window** , open **Settings → Channels → Messenger Live Chat → Overview** . On the **Website** card, choose **Install on website** . If your workspace has the earlier installer, open **Settings → Messenger → Install → Install for web** .[Intercom’s Messenger installation guide](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/16946116-new-messenger-install-experience-on-your-website)


From Settings → Channels, open Messenger Live Chat. In Overview, choose Install on website in the Website card.


1. Select **Visitors & leads** and click **Continue** .


Select Visitors & leads on the left, then Continue at the bottom of the installation panel.


1. Open the **Install method** menu and choose **Code snippet** under **Custom code** .


Open Install method. Under Custom code, select Code snippet.


1. In **Install for visitors & leads** , find **2. Choose how to add the code** above the code blocks. Open its dropdown and choose the plain JavaScript option. Click **Copy code** when you see the visitor` <script>` snippet. In the kit’s` index.html` , paste it at the marked line immediately before` </body>` and save.


In the second section, open the selector showing NPM package and choose plain JavaScript. Copy the visitor script displayed for that method.


1. In a terminal, open the unzipped folder and start the page with the command below. On Windows, you can use` py` in place of` python3` .


```text
python3   -m   http.server   8000   --bind   127.0.0.1
```


If your installer shows **Enable user traffic for Messenger** , turn it on in the demo workspace. Open` http://127.0.0.1:8000/` in a separate browser profile for the rider. If the workspace has a trusted-domain list, append the bare` 127.0.0.1` under **Messenger → General → Keep your Messenger secure** . An empty list already allows the test page.[Intercom’s web installation settings](https://developers.intercom.com/installing-intercom/web/installation) ·[Intercom trusted domains](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/4418-list-trusted-domains-you-use-with-your-messenger)


Open the Messenger launcher. Back in the installer, find **Test your installation** and select **Test installation** . **Messenger is installed** confirms that Intercom detected the widget. Keep the rider’s window open. In step 3 you’ll send a real question from it and find the same words in the shop’s Inbox.


*When the blue launcher appears on the shop page, open it in the rider’s browser. The next message you type there will arrive in the owner’s Intercom Inbox.*


## 2. How do you connect the right Quickchat AI Agent to Intercom?


Start with a question the shop can answer the same way every time. Any rider can learn the Saturday hours. Only someone at the shop can agree to have a particular bicycle ready on Friday. Put the hours in the Agent’s **Knowledge Base** and tell it who can make an exception in its **Main Prompt** .


### Give the Agent its Saturday pickup policy


1. Open Quickchat AI with a demo account. On **Getting Started** , choose **Set up manually** , then enter **Wheelhouse Repair** as the Agent’s name under **Identity** . If you already have a demo Agent, select it at the top left. Quickchat AI’s Free plan includes Intercom and Human Handoff for personal learning. AI replies use credits, and commercial use requires a paid plan.[Create an account](https://app.quickchat.ai/register) ·[Dashboard quickstart](https://quickchat.ai/docs/quickstart) ·[Quickchat AI plans](https://quickchat.ai/pricing)
2. Select **Knowledge Base** in the left sidebar. On the dashboard, click the **Add Article** card.


Choose Knowledge Base in the left sidebar, then Add Article in the top row. After saving, look for Ready beside Saturday pickup.


1. Enter **Saturday pickup** in **Title** , paste this policy into **Content** and choose **Save** . Wait for **Ready** in the article list.


```text
Customers can collect completed bicycles from Wheelhouse Repair on Saturdays from 10:00 to 13:00 local time. Only a shop teammate can review a request to collect a bicycle outside that window. The shop has no automatic booking or rescheduling service.
```


Enter the title and policy in the Edit Article panel, then click Save at the top right.


1. Open **Identity → AI Persona → Main Prompt** . Enter these instructions and allow the edit to save.


```text
You are the support assistant for Wheelhouse Repair. Give pickup hours from the Knowledge Base. If the visitor wants a person or asks to change a pickup, offer a human handoff. Never confirm a booking or a change yourself.
```


In Identity, keep AI Persona selected. Click Edit on the right side of the Main Prompt row.


Select **AI Preview** near the top of the Agent’s left sidebar, above **Conversations** . In the preview chat, ask “When can I collect my bike on Saturday?” Our local Agent answered, “You can collect your bike on Saturday from 10:00 to 13:00 local time.” Check both ends of the window before connecting the channel.


*This is the answer to look for again when you assign the rider’s first Messenger message to the AI.*


### Connect the teammate who will sign the AI replies


1. Stay in the browser signed into Intercom as the **Quickchat AI** teammate. In a new tab, sign in to the Quickchat AI account that owns the demo Agent. The two products can use different email addresses. Look at the **Agent selector at the top left** . Choose **Wheelhouse Repair** and open **Knowledge Base** . Seeing **Saturday pickup** here tells you which Agent will supply the shop’s answer.
2. Open **External Apps** in the Agent’s sidebar and choose **Intercom** .


Select External Apps in the left sidebar. In this desktop layout, Intercom is the third card in the second row.


1. In the Intercom panel, click **Connect to Intercom** .


With Wheelhouse Repair selected, click Connect to Intercom in the panel on the right.


1. On Intercom’s consent screen, read the workspace name beside **Quickchat AI wants to access** . Our screen showed **Wheelhouse Repair** and listed access to conversations, teams and teammates, data attributes and AI content. Review the request and click **Authorize access** .[Quickchat AI’s Intercom channel guide](https://quickchat.ai/docs/channels/intercom)


Check the workspace name above the permissions. Select Authorize access at the bottom to connect this workspace.


1. Back in Quickchat AI, our Wheelhouse Repair panel showed **Connected** , **Enabled** and **Connected as Quickchat AI** . Human handoff was still off, and inactive chats would close after ten minutes. Use these four settings so the shop has time to take the Friday request. Each change saves as you make it.[Full Intercom setup walkthrough](https://quickchat.ai/post/create-an-ai-chatbot-for-intercom-quickchat-ai-integration)


After authorization, find the two lower settings in the right-hand panel. Enable human handoff and change the inactivity timeout to Never. Setting Value for the pickup test What the rider or shop should see


Enable Intercom On The channel can receive the rider’s Messenger question.


Reply to all conversations Off The AI answers after the shop assigns it the conversation.


Offer human handoff to Intercom admins On A confirmed transfer can release the AI’s individual assignment.


Automatically close inactive conversations Never The thread stays open while the rider and the shop switch windows.


1. Click **Test connection** . Our green confirmation read **“Connection is valid. Authenticated as Quickchat AI.”** That tells us which Intercom teammate will speak for the Agent. To see it answer a customer, we’ll give that teammate the rider’s first question in the next step.


Click Test connection below Connected as. The green result appeared at the bottom right after the settings were saved.


### What if the Connect to Intercom button is missing?


We ran into this when the Agent picker was set to a different demo Agent. It already had a saved connection, so the panel offered **Reconnect** . Even with **Enable Intercom** off, that Agent showed both **Connected** and **Disabled** .


An Agent with saved credentials shows Reconnect in the Connect section. Check the badges at the top and the teammate under Connected as.


Close the panel with **×** , click the Agent name at the top left and search for **Wheelhouse** . Choose **Wheelhouse Repair** , check for **Saturday pickup** in its Knowledge Base and reopen **External Apps → Intercom** . A new connection begins with **Connect to Intercom** . If the intended Agent already shows **Connected as Quickchat AI** , use **Test connection** . If it shows the human owner, sign into Intercom as the dedicated teammate in this browser profile, then choose **Reconnect** .


## 3. How do you assign a Messenger conversation to the AI?


Start in the **rider’s browser** . Click the blue chat bubble at the bottom right of the shop page. In our visitor session it opened straight to **Wheelhouse Repair** with an empty **Message…** field. If your Messenger opens to a home screen, choose **Send us a message** . Ask **“When can I collect my bike on Saturday?”** and keep that window open.


The rider stays on the shop page. Open the blue launcher at the lower right and send the Saturday question from its message field.


Messenger showed Wheelhouse Repair’s reply-time estimate, an optional email field and **Waiting for a teammate** . Our rider left the field empty. The Saturday question was already in the shop’s Inbox, ready for us to assign.[Intercom’s simple automations](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/7836462-simple-automations-explained)


Switch to the **owner’s Intercom Inbox** . Choose **All** from the left sidebar to see the shop’s conversations. Before the rider wrote, my personal inbox showed **0 Open** and **All** showed four.[How Intercom’s Inbox views work](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6588834-organize-your-inbox-with-custom-views-and-folders)


In the shop owner’s Inbox, use All in the left sidebar to see conversations that have yet to be assigned to a teammate.


The rider’s message brought **All** to five. Open the row with the words you just typed, **“When can I collect my bike on Saturday?”** An anonymous rider may have a name you don’t recognize.


Match the rider’s question in All, then look in Details on the right. Click the individual Assignee value above Team Inbox.


In the **Details** pane on the right, both **Assignee** and **Team Inbox** read **Unassigned** in our trial. Click the **Assignee** value or press **A** while the conversation is selected and the cursor is outside the reply box. In **Assign to** , choose the individual **Quickchat AI** teammate. Now **Assignee** reads **Quickchat AI** and **Team Inbox** still reads **Unassigned** . Assigning to a team instead clears the individual assignee, which matters when the AI only answers its own chats.[Assign conversations to teammates and teams](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6561699-assign-conversations-to-teammates-and-teams)


In Assign to, select the individual teammate named Quickchat AI. Back in Details, Team Inbox can still read Unassigned.


Return to the **rider’s original Messenger** . Ours showed **“Quickchat joined the conversation”** , then **“You can collect your bike on Saturday from 10:00 to 13:00 local time.”** The visitor saw the name **Quickchat** . The shop saw **Quickchat AI** in Details. The Quickchat AI transcript contained just two messages. Assigning the chat picked up the rider’s original question.


*One answer from both sides of the counter. The owner first saw Not seen under the blue reply. After the rider opened the conversation, the same reply showed Seen.*


The yellow note beneath the owner’s reply links staff to the Quickchat AI transcript. The rider sees the public reply in Messenger. Keep that thread open for the question only the shop can answer.[How Intercom’s seen states work](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/258-real-time-messaging-explained)


## 4. How does Quickchat AI hand off an Intercom conversation?


Keep the rider’s Saturday conversation open. You’re about to give the Agent a rule for the moment the rider asks for an exception. You’ll know it worked when the rider sees a transfer message **and** the AI’s name comes off the conversation in Intercom.


1. In Quickchat AI, open **Actions & MCPs** , turn on **Human Handoff** and choose **Edit Action** .


Under Actions & MCPs, find Human Handoff. Its switch is at the top right of the card and Edit Action is below.


1. Open **Handoff rules** and click **+** . In the new row enter the rule name and description below, then turn on **State** .


Click + beside State to open a blank row. The shop’s saved Pickup Change rule is above it. If yours already exists, edit that row. Field Value to use


Rule Name Pickup Change


Description The visitor asks to change an existing bike pickup or explicitly asks for a person. A request for the published pickup hours can be answered from the Knowledge Base.


Question Would you like a shop teammate to take over here?


Confirmation I’m passing this conversation to the shop team. They can read our messages here.


Turn on State for Pickup Change after entering its description. The switch applies to this rule.


1. Open **Question** and **Confirmation** in the same editor. Paste each message into its own field and select **Save** . If the Agent uses an availability schedule, run the test during its staffed hours. A matched rule can produce a confirmation in the Agent’s own words.[Human Handoff settings](https://quickchat.ai/docs/ai-agent/actions/human-handoff)


Use the Question and Confirmation fields in the same editor. Click Save at the top right when both messages are in place.


1. In the **owner’s Intercom Inbox** , open the conversation header’s **⋯ → Show conversation events** and select **Assignment** .[Show assignment events in the Inbox](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/13334840-conversation-events-in-the-inbox)


Open the conversation’s top menu, choose Show conversation events and check Assignment. Keep the filter on for the Friday request.


The assignment event appears in the conversation itself. Details on the right shows Quickchat AI as its current owner.


1. Back in the same visitor thread, ask **“Can I collect my bike on Friday instead? Please pass this to a person.”** If the Agent asks whether to transfer, reply **“Yes, please.”**


Our rider asked for a person **once** . Quickchat AI answered, **“I’ve passed your request to a person who can help with changing your pickup to Friday.”** The next Inbox event read **“Quickchat AI unassigned the teammate”** . Before anyone at the shop claimed the chat, **Details → Assignee** and **Team Inbox** both read **Unassigned** .


*The confirmation tells the rider what happened. The event and the two Unassigned rows show the shop where the conversation went.*


Read the event **before you claim the conversation** . The earlier **“You assigned Quickchat AI”** belongs to the Saturday question. If your workspace routes the Friday request straight to another teammate or team, the later events will show that destination.


If the thread disappears from the AI’s personal inbox, open **All** and find the Friday question. Look at **Assignee** and **Team Inbox** separately. The sidebar’s **Unassigned** view only includes items that have neither a teammate nor a team. In our workspace the chat waited there until I claimed it. In a shared queue, agree who watches that view or the team inbox your routing sends it to.[Intercom’s Unassigned view](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6588834-organize-your-inbox-with-custom-views-and-folders)


## 5. How does a human take over in Intercom Inbox?


In the **owner’s Intercom Inbox** , click the **Assignee** value or press **A** outside the reply box. In **Assign to** , choose **You** . Intercom recorded **“You assigned yourself”** when I did this. My name appeared under **Details → Assignee** while **Team Inbox** stayed **Unassigned** .


After Quickchat AI releases the chat, choose You in Assign to. Your own name should appear under Assignee on the right.


Read the rider’s Friday request, choose **Reply** in the composer and send **“I can see your Friday request. Before I check it, which collection time were you hoping for?”** Keep the conversation open.[Intercom’s guide to replies and notes](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6525765-loop-teammates-or-teams-into-conversations)


Use Reply at the bottom of the conversation, then Send. A Note is visible only to teammates.


Switch back to **the rider’s original Messenger** . The Friday reply appeared under **Piotr** , just below **“Piotr joined the conversation”** . The owner’s first screenshot showed **Not seen** under the sent message. The rider’s screenshot at the top of this guide shows where the public reply landed.


*Use Reply to reach the rider. The same message first showed Not seen in the Inbox and later showed Seen after the rider opened the conversation.*


### Check who answers after the handoff


Our rider wrote **“Around 16:00, please. Is that possible?”** I answered from the shop’s Inbox **about 1 minute 38 seconds later** , asking whether 16:30 would work. No AI message appeared between us. The rider saw **Piotr** under my question and Intercom still showed me as the individual **Assignee** .


*In the rider’s window, 16:00 is the outgoing blue message. The 16:30 question arrived from Piotr. On the shop’s side, that same question is the outgoing reply marked Seen.*


To continue the negotiation, send **“Yes, 16:30 works for me too. Could the shop check both times?”** from **Message…** on the bike page. The rider’s follow-up should appear in the shop’s Inbox with the human still assigned. The shop can then answer from **Reply** .


### Compare the same Saturday question with two different assignees


We already knew the Agent could answer **“When can I collect my bike on Saturday?”** We asked those exact words in two fresh conversations. This time the rider opened each chat with **Hello** so I could assign it *before* the pickup question arrived.


**Give the first chat to Quickchat AI.** Open the new **Hello** in **Inbox → All** , click the individual **Assignee** and choose **Quickchat AI** . Messenger had already shown the rider the shop’s reply-time estimate and contact prompt. After I made the assignment, the rider saw **Quickchat joined the conversation** and received **“Hello! How can I help you today?”**


*The shop picked the individual teammate named Quickchat AI. The rider saw the shorter name Quickchat beneath the greeting.*


The rider sent the Saturday question and estimated that this answer appeared in Messenger about 10 seconds later.


> You can collect your bike on Saturday from 10:00 to 13:00 local time.


**Give the second chat to yourself.** In Chrome, choose **Profile → Add Chrome profile** , open the same shop page and send **Hello** . In your existing **Inbox → All** , open that greeting and choose **Assignee → You** . I saw **You assigned yourself** in the timeline and my name under **Assignee** .[Chrome profiles](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/2364824?hl=en)


From that rider’s Messenger, send the same Saturday question. Leave the shop’s **Reply** box empty for two minutes. Our rider saw **Waiting for a teammate** after sending. In my Inbox, the question went from **Now** to **2m** in two screenshots taken **2 minutes 4 seconds apart** . It was still the last public message, and I was still assigned.


Assigned to Quickchat AI. The rider received the hours. The shop saw the same answer marked Seen.


Assigned to Piotr. Messenger shows the rider’s view just after sending. The later Inbox view shows the question still waiting for the shop.


### When the rider comes back to an empty Messenger


When we returned to the bike page after the Friday exchange, **Messages** said **No messages** . Clicking **Send us a message** opened a blank composer. The Wheelhouse Repair Agent’s saved Intercom conversation was still open with all seven messages, ending with my question about 16:30.


The rider’s Messages tab was empty on return. Send us a message opens a new conversation.


In a blank composer, use the back arrow beside the shop name to return to Messages and look for the thread containing the 16:30 reply.


1. **Rider.** Return to the original tab or open the same address in the same browser profile. Our kit uses` http://127.0.0.1:8000/` . Intercom uses a first-party cookie to recognize an anonymous visitor. In **Messages** , look for the blue **“Around 16:00, please”** followed by Piotr’s reply. Send the next rider message there.[Intercom Messenger cookies](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/2361922-intercom-messenger-cookies)
2. **Shop.** Open **Inbox → Search** and enter **“which collection time were you hoping for”** . The result lets you read the Friday exchange and check **Details → Assignee** , even when the visitor’s browser shows an empty composer.[Intercom Inbox search](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6516006-inbox-search-and-filter)


### Where did the handoff stop?


What you see What to try next


The bike page opens without a chat bubble. Check that web Messenger traffic is enabled in the selected workspace. Under **Settings → Channels → Messenger → Widget → Show the Messenger Launcher** , include **Visitors** and check that the shop page matches any display conditions. Refresh the rider’s page.[Intercom’s launcher settings](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/1155368-control-who-can-see-the-messenger-launcher-on-your-site)


Messenger opens, but the rider can’t start a conversation. Under **Settings → Channels → Messenger → General → Control inbound volume** , check **Let visitors start a conversation** and any display conditions for the shop page. Refresh the rider’s page after saving.[Intercom’s inbound conversation controls](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/3941657-control-inbound-conversation-volume)


The AI never answers the first hours question. Match **Connected as** to the individual **Assignee** , test the channel connection and check the Agent’s credits. Confirm the article is Ready.


Every mention of pickup goes to a human. Ask the hours question and the Friday-change question in separate fresh chats assigned to the AI. Narrow the rule to changes and requests for a person, then repeat both.


The AI replies after Piotr takes over. Check **Reply to all conversations** and turn on **Workflows & actions** in the event menu. Look for a later assignment back to the AI teammate. If a workflow routed the chat back, limit its trigger to the first message from your test audience.


Piotr can see the reply in Inbox but the rider cannot. Check whether Piotr sent a **Note** . Switch to **Reply** , send a public message and reopen the original visitor thread.


### Why did the correct Saturday answer score 2 out of 5?


Our first run in **Conversations → Testing** gave both replies **2/5** . The Agent had answered the hours question and offered a human for Friday. Our evaluation criteria said, “Give the Saturday hours. Offer a human for a pickup change. Never confirm a booking.” The evaluator expected each reply to do both jobs. It wanted the Saturday answer to offer a person and the Friday answer to include Saturday’s hours.


To repeat the comparison, open **Conversations → Testing** and click **Create Dataset** .


Open Testing under Conversations, then click Create Dataset beside the page title.


Choose **Paste messages** , name the dataset **Wheelhouse pickup handoff** and paste these two messages. The line between them makes them separate test cases.


```text
What is your Saturday pickup window?
---
Can I collect my bike on Friday instead? Please pass this to a person.
```


Select Paste messages in the new panel. The two-message count sits below the prompts, and Evaluation criteria opens underneath.


Under **Evaluation criteria** , give each question its own condition. Here is the rubric we used for the second run.


```text
Grade each message independently. For a request for Saturday pickup hours, a full answer gives 10:00 to 13:00 local time; no handoff is needed. For a request to change pickup to Friday or reach a person, a full answer offers or initiates a human transfer without confirming a booking; no hours are needed. Apply only the relevant case.
```


Create the dataset and choose **Run** .


Open the saved Wheelhouse pickup handoff dataset. Click Run in the upper-right corner above its two messages.


In **Start Test Run** , review the credit estimate for the two messages and click **Start Run** .


After Run, the centered dialog shows the estimate. Choose Start Run to carry out the test.


With the same Agent settings and the same two visitor messages, the new run scored **5/5 on each reply** . The grader’s explanation now connected each answer to the right request. Use this check for wording. The Friday thread in Intercom is where you verify the assignee and delivery.[Simulation Testing](https://quickchat.ai/docs/conversations/testing)


Both runs used the same Agent and prompts. Applying the appropriate criterion to each request raised the two scores from 2/5 to 5/5.


To use this in your own queue, pick two questions that sound alike but need different owners. “When do refunds arrive?” has a policy answer. “Can you approve my refund?” needs a person who can make that decision. Run both through the same Messenger. For the second one, finish on the customer’s side and read the teammate’s reply. For out-of-hours requests and returning a chat to the AI, see the[human handoff workflow guide](https://quickchat.ai/post/chatbot-human-handoff-workflow) .


## Frequently asked questions


### How does a Quickchat AI chatbot hand a conversation to a human in Intercom?


Connect Quickchat AI as a dedicated Intercom teammate, turn off Reply to all conversations and turn on Offer human handoff to Intercom admins. Enable the Agent’s Human Handoff action. In our test the AI confirmed the transfer and released its individual assignment. Piotr claimed the open conversation in Intercom Inbox, read the Friday request and replied in the rider’s original Messenger thread.


### How do I change the chatbot teammate’s name in Intercom Inbox?


Sign in as the dedicated Intercom teammate and open Settings → Personal → Details. Click Edit on the profile, replace the name beside the person icon and click Done. Refresh the Teammates list to check the name you can search for under Assign to. A customer-facing alias keeps the existing name in the assignment menu.


### Can I test the handoff before paying for Intercom seats?


Yes. We used two full seats on Intercom’s 14-day Essential trial, one for the shop owner and one for the AI teammate. Intercom lets you add seats during the trial without a credit card. To keep Messenger live afterward, choose a paid plan and allow for both full seats.


### When is Quickchat AI cheaper than Intercom Fin?


Intercom Fin charges[$0.99 per resolution](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/8205718-fin-ai-agent-outcomes) . Quickchat AI Enterprise starts at[$0.50 per resolution](https://quickchat.ai/pricing#pricing) with a minimum of 2,000 resolutions per month. That starting rate is about 49% lower.


Suppose 100 riders each ask for Saturday hours and one AI reply resolves each chat. At regular US monthly rates, the shop would pay **$87** for Quickchat AI Starter ($9) and[two $39 Intercom Essential seats](https://www.intercom.com/learning-center/intercom-pricing) , one for the owner and one for the AI teammate. At[one credit per reply](https://quickchat.ai/docs/understanding-ai-credits) , those 100 answers fit within Starter’s 150 monthly credits. With Fin, one $39 seat and 100 resolutions come to **$138** . If a rider simply asks for a person, Fin can hand off without an outcome charge. Read our[Quickchat AI vs. Intercom Fin comparison](https://quickchat.ai/post/best-intercom-fin-alternatives#intercom-fin-vs-quickchat-ai) .


### Can I test Intercom Messenger locally before adding it to my website?


Yes. Serve a page containing the demo workspace’s visitor snippet on your computer and open` http://127.0.0.1:8000/` in a visitor browser. If the workspace restricts trusted domains, add` 127.0.0.1` to the list. We opened the real Wheelhouse Repair Messenger this way. Send a visitor question from the page and open that conversation in Intercom Inbox to test assignment and replies.


### Why does Test connection pass when my Intercom chatbot still won’t hand off?


Test connection verifies the Intercom credentials and reports the authenticated teammate. In Quickchat AI, select the Agent that holds your support policy, open its Intercom channel and turn on Offer human handoff to Intercom admins. Enable the Agent’s Human Handoff action too. Then assign a live Messenger conversation to that teammate and watch its assignment history when the visitor asks for a person.


### Why do I see Reconnect instead of Connect to Intercom?


Reconnect means the selected Quickchat AI Agent already has a saved Intercom connection, even if its channel is disabled. Check the Agent’s name at the top left and the teammate beside Connected as. If both are correct, use Test connection. If you chose a different Agent, switch to the Agent with your support article and open External Apps → Intercom there.


### How do I stop Quickchat AI replying after I take over in Intercom?


Turn off Reply to all conversations in Quickchat AI’s Intercom settings. Claim the open chat and confirm your name under Details → Assignee. To test it, ask a question from the visitor’s Messenger and leave the human’s Reply box empty. In our test the Saturday pickup question stayed unanswered in Piotr’s Inbox for more than two minutes. If the AI replies, check the assignment history and any workflows that route new messages back to it.


### Does moving a chat to a team inbox assign it to a specific teammate?


Intercom tracks the team and the individual assignee separately. Assigning a conversation to a team clears its individual assignment. Choosing a teammate keeps the team assignment in place. In assigned-only mode, Quickchat AI checks the individual teammate.


### Why does Your inbox show 0 Open when All shows conversations in Intercom?


Your inbox shows conversations assigned to you. The count beside All includes open conversations and tickets across teammate and team assignments. Open All and look for the visitor’s exact message. Then check the individual Assignee in Details.


### Why is a handed-off conversation missing from the Unassigned view in Intercom?


The Unassigned view counts open conversations and tickets that have neither a teammate nor a team. A conversation can lose its individual assignee and still belong to a team. Find it in All, open Details and check both Assignee and Team Inbox. Show Assignment events to see who owned it before and after the handoff.


### Do I need an Intercom Workflow to test chatbot handoff?


You can assign the first Messenger question to the Quickchat AI teammate yourself in Intercom Inbox. That’s how we tested the handoff on Essential. To automate that first assignment, use the Workflows builder on Advanced or Expert. Route the first message from your chosen audience to the dedicated teammate.


### Why does Intercom Messenger ask for my email before Quickchat AI answers?


Intercom can show the team’s expected reply time and ask for contact details when a conversation starts. Our rider left the email field empty. Their question was already in the shop’s Inbox, and assigning the conversation to Quickchat AI let the Agent answer in the same thread.


### Which inbox shows who owns the conversation after an Intercom handoff?


In Intercom Inbox, open Details and check Assignee. Show Assignment events to see how the chat got there. In our test, Intercom recorded “You assigned yourself” and showed Piotr as the assignee. The Quickchat AI transcript recorded the human reply and still showed Open and Unassigned in its own inbox.


### How can I tell whether a customer received my human reply?


Use the public Reply composer in Intercom Inbox, then open the same conversation in the visitor’s Messenger. Match the words and the name beneath the message. Our rider saw the 16:30 question under Piotr’s name. The Inbox first marked that reply Not seen and later showed Seen. An internal Note stays in the Inbox.


### Why does Intercom Messenger say “No messages” when the team can still see the conversation?


An anonymous visitor’s Messenger uses a cookie to retrieve their history. Open the same shop address in the original rider’s browser profile, then look in Messages for the teammate’s last reply. On the team side, search Intercom Inbox for a phrase from the conversation to find its transcript and check its assignee.
